claim_text: The Minnesota Office of the Legislative Auditor found that MDE's inadequate oversight of Feeding Our Future created opportunities for fraud. OLA did not find that MDE officials themselves stole funds or were charged with crimes.
normalized_claim: OLA June 2024: MDE oversight failure created opportunities for fraud (actor classes B/C, not D).

amounts.methodology: OLA transmittal recites federal charging of a $250 million fraud scheme as the federal government's allegation, not an OLA-audited loss total

supporting_passages.quote: MDE’s inadequate oversight of Feeding Our Future created opportunities for fraud.
MDE’s only administrative review of Feeding Our Future’s CACFP operations—conducted in 2018—resulted in serious findings that required follow-up, but MDE never conducted a follow-up review.
Between June 2018 and December 2021, the Minnesota Department of Education (MDE) received at least 30 complaints involving Feeding Our Future or its sites.
Most importantly, MDE had reason to doubt Feeding Our Future’s trustworthiness as a sponsor, yet MDE continued to ask Feeding Our Future to resolve complaints about itself.

More broadly, despite repeated warnings by the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA’s) Office of Inspector General of the risks of fraud, waste, and abuse in federal nutrition programs, MDE was not prepared to investigate these issues in CACFP or SFSP.

Finally, MDE officials told us that the department met the federal requirement to inform USDA of “any suspected fraud or criminal abuse…which would result in a loss or misuse of Federal funds” in SFSP when it shared its concerns about Feeding Our Future with USDA’s Office of Inspector General in October or November 2020. However, informing USDA of its concerns did not absolve MDE of its legal responsibility to (1) “promptly investigate” program-related complaints and irregularities, and (2) “take appropriate action to correct any irregularities” in CACFP and SFSP.
While MDE had written complaint investigation procedures, their limited scope and failure to address important issues undermined their ability to promote good investigative practices.
MDE did not investigate some complaints about Feeding Our Future, despite their frequency or seriousness.
MDE inappropriately asked Feeding Our Future to investigate complaints about itself.
When MDE decided to investigate complaints about Feeding Our Future, the investigations were inadequate.
MDE’s inadequate oversight of Feeding Our Future created opportunities for fraud.
However, we found MDE’s oversight of Feeding Our Future to be inadequate. In fact, we believe MDE’s actions and inactions created opportunities for fraud.

qualifiers: OLA findings are audit conclusions about oversight (B/C), not criminal charges against MDE (not D).
MDE written dispute exists (Commissioner Willie L. Jett II letter 2024-06-07); see fof-c-018.
OLA transmittal recites federal charging of 70 individuals and a $250 million scheme as DOJ's allegation.

assertion_ladder.current_assessment: Strong evidence of oversight failure (B) and being ill-prepared / using untrained investigators / asking FOF to investigate itself (C). Insufficient evidence for official misconduct (D) or government criminal participation (E).

editorial_notes: Actor class B and C. Not D. Do not collapse B/C into D.

claim_text: In a September 23, 2022, Minnesota Judicial Branch statement, the court stated that Judge John Guthmann never ordered MDE to resume payments to Feeding Our Future in April 2021 or at any other time, and that MDE voluntarily resumed payments.

supporting_passages.quote: Judge Guthmann never ordered the Department of Education to resume payments to FOF in April 2021, or at any other time.
Thereafter, the Department of Education voluntarily resumed making payments to FOF. The Department of Education was not ordered by the court to do so.
All of the MN Department of Education food reimbursement payments to FOF were made voluntarily, without any court order.

qualifiers: Court's own statement of the public court record, not a criminal adjudication.
Consent order Dec 22, 2020 concerned processing applications (not payments).

editorial_notes: Distinguishes B/C oversight and civil-procedure disputes from D. The statement calls the Star Tribune line that Guthmann ordered the department to resume payments, the commissioner's April 4, 2022 Senate testimony to that effect, and Governor Walz's September 22, 2022 media comments false.

claim_text: This collection found no USDA OIG audit, investigation report, or press release that independently quantifies Minnesota CACFP/SFSP Feeding Our Future losses. What exists is OLA's account that MDE referred concerns to USDA OIG in October or November 2020; a 2024 House Education and the Workforce subpoena to USDA OIG; and FNS national integrity rulemaking citing older (2011/2013) OIG work unrelated to Minnesota FOF.

supporting_passages.quote: MDE officials told us that the department met the federal requirement to inform USDA of “any suspected fraud or criminal abuse…which would result in a loss or misuse of Federal funds” in SFSP when it shared its concerns about Feeding Our Future with USDA’s Office of Inspector General in October or November 2020.

qualifiers: Gap as to USDA-OIG work product, not a finding that OIG did nothing.
OLA reports MDE's claim that it informed USDA OIG; OLA does not independently audit USDA OIG's response beyond recording MDE's account and stating that a referral did not discharge MDE's own duties.
Journalism quotes attributing an 'emboldened' sentence to Emily Honer are a lead unless quoted from the OLA PDF itself.
